stories.label: Saudi Arabia reports interception of Houthi drone targeting Mecca
stories.summary: The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted and destroyed a drone launched toward the Mecca region on Friday morning; the Houthis deny aiming at the holy city's region. Lead with the claim and the denial, attributed to each side and stated as neither fact: no one independent has confirmed the target. The new development on the Yemen arc is the war's rhetoric reaching Islam's holiest city, in a conflict that has displaced more than 280,000 Yemenis. Say who gains from the framing and what it means for civilians on both sides of the border.

stories.label: 'Don't Be Loud, Don't Make Noise': Pentagon Tells European Allies To Tone Down Russia Rhetoric
stories.summary: Pentagon officials have asked Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, among other NATO governments, to soften how they talk about the threat from Russia, according to four people cited in the report. Lead with the instruction itself: the states on Russia's border are being told by their guarantor to be quiet. The mechanism is the leverage a security guarantee gives its provider over an ally's speech. Datelined where it lands, in the Baltics. Keep the anonymous sourcing visible.

stories.label: Bolivian Attorney General Was Arrested After Investigating Trump-Aligned Operative
stories.summary: Drop Site reports that Bolivia's attorney general was arrested after investigating Fernando Cerimedo, an operative aligned with Trump. Lead with that sequence, and name who ordered the arrest and on what charge. The structural point is selective use of drug-trafficking accusations to advance US interests in Latin America: an accusation that can remove the person doing the investigating. Single-outlet reporting, so attribute the link between the probe and the arrest to Drop Site rather than stating it as fact.

stories.label: Canada's economic break with the US in 5 charts
stories.summary: Carney hosts EU leaders in Montreal on Friday as von der Leyen says the EU is considering Canada as an associate member, despite opposition inside the bloc. Lead with the associate-membership idea: the closest US trading partner is looking across the Atlantic because of Trump's trade pressure. Use the trade figures to show how far the break has actually gone, and say what associate status would and would not give Canada, and who in Europe objects.

stories.label: Hong Kong's wider yuan push: a gateway to the world?
stories.summary: The African Export-Import Bank is planning a $1 billion three-year syndicated loan that could include an offshore yuan tranche, its first foray into the offshore renminbi market, according to people familiar with the matter. Lead with Afreximbank, not with Hong Kong: Africa's trade bank borrowing in the yuan as China-Africa trade grows. Use the South China Morning Post piece for Hong Kong's push to be the channel for it. Name the yuan as the series, and be plain that the loan is planned and the tranche is not settled.

stories.label: 📉 Earnings Snippet: Amazon's Pain Points
stories.summary: AI revenue is rising and it did not protect Amazon or Alphabet from a Wall Street sell-off after their results; Amazon's AI build-out pushed its cash burn to a record. Lead with that record cash burn and what it was spent on. The mechanism: the bill for AI data centres is now arriving faster than the revenue, and investors have started pricing that. Intel was covered this morning, so keep it to one clause and make this the capital-spending story.

stories.label: 刚刚，梁文锋千亿融资细节曝光：近30家机构，腾讯宁王领跑，国资占比27%
stories.summary: DeepSeek has raised 105.5 billion yuan (about $15.8 billion) from nearly 30 investors, and Chinese state investors supplied about 27% of it, up from 2% in the first round; The Information reported the figures and Zhidx relayed them, so attribute them that way. Lead with that jump in state money. The mechanism: DeepSeek doubled the round midway as a server with eight Nvidia B300 chips rose from about 15 million to 19 million yuan in four months, over five times the price in most countries, which is what US export controls cost a Chinese lab.

stories.label: 拟融资334亿！英伟达投的大模型独角兽又融资，冲击加拿大史上最大单轮融资纪录
stories.summary: Canada's government will take a stake of up to C$1.6 billion in the AI company Cohere, on terms: at least 1,000 new Canadian technical jobs by 2030, at least C$1.7 billion in local computing, and the headquarters stays in Canada. Lead with the state buying a sovereign AI lab on conditions. The round targets up to C$7 billion, led by Germany's Schwarz Group, with Aramco's Prosperity7 among the backers; the pending Aleph Alpha merger makes Cohere the non-American option for European governments. The agreement was published by the prime minister's office.

stories.label: Europe Begins Funding Offensive In-Space Capabilities
stories.summary: Announcements this week show the European space sector moving from defending satellites to funding the means to act against them. Lead with what was funded, by whom and how much, and what the capability does. The structural shift is Europe's departure from a civil and defensive posture in orbit, where the same rendezvous technology used to clear debris can also reach another country's satellite.

stories.label: The Treatment Window For Some Strokes May Be Far Longer Than We Thought, But There's a Catch
stories.summary: The rule behind stroke care is that time is brain: an estimated 1.9 million neurons lost per minute untreated. New research suggests that for some strokes the window for treatment runs far longer than assumed. Lead with how much longer and for which patients, then the catch, stated as prominently as the finding. Name the study and journal, and who gets left out if the extended window depends on imaging that poorer hospitals lack, if the source supports that.

stories.label: Eating disorders are on the rise. GLP-1s could make things worse.
stories.summary: Emerging evidence suggests some people with eating disorders are misusing GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, and clinical psychologists warn the drugs can act as a trigger. Lead with what the evidence actually measures and how strong it is, keeping it distinct from clinicians' worry. The mechanism: a drug that suppresses appetite is the tool an eating disorder is looking for, and the people prescribing or selling it may not screen for one.

stories.label: Ukraine Pauses Strikes on Russian Refineries After Pressure From U.S.
stories.summary: Kyiv has halted one of its most effective weapons — drone strikes on Russian refineries — after weeks of pressure from Trump, whose concern is the oil price during a Gulf war. Lead with the trade-off: Ukraine gives up leverage over Moscow's war revenue so Washington can keep Brent crude down; who gains is Russia's export budget. Name Brent crude for the chart. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: Venezuela's Machado lauds Trump for 'freedom', urges 2027 elections
stories.summary: Machado says Washington has proposed Venezuelan elections in 2027 — a timetable for the post-Maduro transition set in Washington, not Caracas. Lead with who sets the date: Delcy Rodríguez's interim government, the US, or Venezuelan voters, and Machado's pledge that Venezuela becomes America's 'greatest ally'. Dateline Caracas; continues the Maduro-case watch item.

stories.label: Inside the Syrian Village Hit by Jordan’s Airstrikes
stories.summary: Jordanian jets struck a village in southern Syria in what Amman called a precision strike on the Islamic State; New Lines names the dead — Lamis, 8, Osama, 9, Yaseen, 11, their uncle and grandmother — children whose father had been disappeared by Assad. Lead with the names and the gap between Amman's 'precision' claim and who was killed; ask who investigates cross-border strikes on post-Assad Syria. Dateline the village in southern Syria (Daraa/Suwayda governorate as reported).

stories.label: Binance's possible hack triggers $3 billion freeze in crypto assets
stories.summary: Binance puts the breach at $6.3 billion — likely the largest crypto theft ever — and blockchain sleuths attribute it to North Korea's Lazarus Group. Lead with the split: about $2.5-3 billion was frozen through issuers and partners, but 18,270 bitcoin (~$1.4bn) moved into 19 wallets that nobody can freeze. That is the mechanism — 'decentralised' money is freezable only where a company sits in the middle. Name bitcoin for the chart (down >3% to ~$77,400); deposits and withdrawals remain suspended. Merge CoinDesk's Lazarus attribution and wallet tracing.

stories.label: PC chip plunge wipes out a quarter of Intel's value
stories.summary: Intel lost almost a quarter of its market value in a day after Q3 results showed a deep fall in PC processor sales; its CEO promises a datacentre CPU boom it may lack the production capacity to serve. Lead with the 23% drop and the mechanism: AI spending is flowing to datacentre chips while Intel's fabs can't ship them — the same week rival AMD's shares rose 11.5%. This is also the US government's largest chip stake. Dateline Santa Clara.

stories.label: EU Satellite Imagery Delayed Over Gaza and Parts of West Bank by 24-hours
stories.summary: Bellingcat found that imagery from the ESA's freely available Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellites appears delayed by 24 hours over Gaza and parts of the West Bank — the open data journalists and rights groups use to document destruction. Lead with the delay and the geography it covers; ask who decided, under what rule, and what other areas are treated alike. Echoes the old US Kyl-Bingaman limit on imagery of Israel.

stories.label: 融资数亿元，零一万物要搬去DeepSeek大本营了！
stories.summary: Kai-Fu Lee's 01.AI, once one of China's 'six little dragons' of frontier models, takes several hundred million yuan from Hangzhou city and district state funds and moves its headquarters from Beijing to Hangzhou, home of DeepSeek and Alibaba. Lead with the pivot: a frontier lab turned enterprise-AI contractor, financed by local government, now building Kazakhstan's sovereign Kazakh-language model AlemLLM. Mechanism: Chinese local governments buying AI firms as industrial policy. Dateline Hangzhou.

stories.label: SPECIAL REPORT: What are Nigerians eating? Tracing TELA maize from farms to dinner tables (I)
stories.summary: A 13-month Premium Times investigation traced Nigeria's first genetically modified maize, the insect-resistant Bt TELA variety, from labs to farms, markets and kitchens: adoption is growing, no verified evidence links it to health harm, and most consumers do not know they are eating it. Lead with the gap between the science (no evidence of harm) and the labelling and consent question. Dateline Kano.

stories.label: 280,000+ Yemenis displaced by war; El Salvador surges more troops to Haiti; Russian drone strike kills 14
stories.summary: Write only the Yemen item: more than 280,000 Yemenis displaced by the renewed Saudi–Ansarallah war. Lead with the displacement figure and who counted it, name where people fled from and to, and who is bombing whom. Ignore the Haiti and Ukraine items in the digest (Dnipro was covered today). Dateline in Yemen.

stories.label: EU force helicopter crash in Bosnia kills four Italians
stories.summary: An Italian CH-47 Chinook serving with EUFOR Althea crashed on a training mission in the Brčko district, killing four Italian soldiers and injuring 11. Lead with the toll; explain what EUFOR still does in Bosnia three decades after Dayton and why the mission matters amid secessionist pressure from Republika Srpska.

stories.label: Japan To Assemble AMRAAM Missiles As U.S. Moves To Dramatically Boost AIM-120 Production
stories.summary: Japan will assemble AIM-120 AMRAAM air-to-air missiles and help speed SM-3 Block IIA interceptor output, part of a multibillion-dollar US expansion after wars drained stockpiles. The mechanism: Washington is turning Japan's arms-export loosening into a second production line, which ties Tokyo into Taiwan and Gulf contingencies. Dateline Tokyo.

stories.label: In Suriname's Amazon, the Wayana community struggling to keep gold miners at bay
stories.summary: The Wayana of Kawemhakan on the Lawa River are mapping their ancestral land to hold off wildcat gold miners, because Suriname, alone in South America, still does not legally recognise Indigenous land rights. Lead with that legal gap and what the mining (mercury, river damage) costs them. Suriname is an OIC member.

stories.label: Polish MiG-29s, F-16 Cannon Ammo Reportedly Headed To Ukraine As Bitter Warsaw-Kyiv Rift Heals
stories.summary: Poland, which called off its MiG-29 transfer in June after relations with Kyiv soured in the spring, is reportedly sending the jets and F-16 cannon ammunition after all. Attribute as reported, explain what broke the relationship and what mended it. Dateline Warsaw.

stories.label: Govt ups high-speed diesel rate by Re0.85 as petrol rate remains at Rs377.91
stories.summary: Pakistan's diesel now retails above Rs400 a litre (Rs400.67), with petrol held at Rs377.91. Diesel moves trucks, tractors and food prices, so the farmer and the transporter pay first. Tie it to Brent crude and the Iran war's effect on Gulf supply, and say how much of the pump price is the government's petroleum levy. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Bitcoin turns 18 this weekend as the world economy gets drunk on crypto
stories.summary: Eighteen years after the white paper, crypto is a $101 billion regional economy in sub-Saharan Africa, but mostly as dollar stablecoins, not the peer-to-peer cash Nakamoto described. Lead with the $101 billion and why Africans use it (weak currencies, remittance costs); bitcoin itself is near $80,000. Dateline Johannesburg.

stories.label: ANALYSIS: Dig first, find water later: Limpopo's industrial insanity
stories.summary: South Africa is planning a coal, coke and steel complex in water-scarce northern Limpopo while the world already has more steelmaking capacity than it needs. Lead with the water the plants need against what the region has, and name who backs the project and who loses the water (farmers, communities). Report the facts, not the analysis's adjectives. Dateline Musina.

stories.label: The Tropical Forest Forever Facility turns one
stories.summary: Brazil's fund to pay tropical countries for standing forest has a charter, a board and a World Bank home a year after launch, but far less money than it promised. Lead with pledged versus target capital, and who would be paid (Congo Basin, Indonesia, Amazon states) once it disburses. Dateline Brasília.

stories.label: Reddit will require you to log in eventually, CEO confirms
stories.summary: Steve Huffman told shareholders Reddit is moving to logged-in-only access after search traffic fell 'meaningfully' as AI answers stop sending clicks. The mechanism: the open web's best-known forum is walling itself off, both to keep AI scrapers out and to sell its data to them. US pick 1 of 3.

stories.label: Trump declares robot imports a national security threat
stories.summary: A Section 232 finding names foreign factory robots a national security threat, ordering trade talks and threatening tariffs. Lead with who makes the robots US factories buy (Japan's Fanuc and Yaskawa, Germany's KUKA under Chinese ownership, China's makers) and the contradiction: tariffs on the tools of the reshoring the policy wants. US pick 2 of 3.

stories.label: Pentagon IG refuses to investigate Starlink/Starshield slowdown in Ukraine
stories.summary: New decision on the Starlink arc: the Pentagon inspector general declined a bipartisan senators' request to investigate SpaceX's restrictions on Ukraine's military use of Starlink and Starshield. Lead with the refusal: a private company's throttling of a war's communications now has no oversight. US pick 3 of 3.

stories.label: Experts: What China wants from the COP31 climate talks
stories.summary: Ahead of COP31 in Turkey, China, the largest emitter and the largest maker of clean technology, is the delegation everyone is watching. Lead with China's emissions trajectory and what it will and will not commit to (finance, its developing-country status, its 2035 target). Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: Borneo's wildfires could have a lasting impact on orangutans
stories.summary: The ecology, not the fire: what researchers know about how peat-fire smoke and habitat loss affect Bornean orangutans (respiratory harm, lost food trees, lower reproduction) during Indonesia's worst El Niño fire season in a decade across Kalimantan. Lead with the research finding. Dateline Palangka Raya.

stories.label: Israel election: Authorities dispute Netanyahu's fraud claims
stories.summary: New development on the coalition arithmetic covered yesterday: Netanyahu and right-wing allies claim Arab parties' record gains came partly from voter fraud and accuse Qatar of interference, and Israel's own Shin Bet now says its foreign-interference probe does not implicate any whole group of voters. Lead with the security service contradicting the prime minister. Who is affected: Palestinian citizens of Israel, whose votes are being cast as illegitimate at the moment they hold the balance of power. Include Doha's denial.

stories.label: Senior US general fired, accused of leaking classified information
stories.summary: Hegseth fired Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, a senior Joint Staff planner, accusing him of leaking classified information, mid-war with Iran and days before the midterms. Lead with the rank: one of the highest-level firings of the war. The mechanism: leak accusations used to remove war planners, with no charges filed. Name what is alleged, who says it, and what due process (if any) applies.

stories.label: Bandits Attack: Reps seek security, humanitarian intervention in Taraba
stories.summary: Between 57 and 60 people were killed in a bandit attack on Binnari community, Karim Lamido LGA, Taraba State, and the House of Representatives is now calling for security and humanitarian intervention. Lead with the death toll; every victim counts as much as in any other war. The structural why: armed banditry spreading from the northwest into the northeast's farming belt while federal security is stretched. Name who failed to protect the village and what lawmakers asked for.

stories.label: The Land Expropriations of the Assad Era Still Hang Over Syria
stories.summary: Farmland outside Damascus seized by the Assad regime was turned into part of a chemical weapons facility, and the families still hold their title deeds. Lead with that detail. The accountability gap: the post-Assad government has offered no restitution for expropriations across Syria, so the old regime's land grabs stand. Who is affected: dispossessed farming families; who holds power: the new authorities in Damascus.

stories.label: In Gaza, Winter Threatens an Already Fragile Power Supply
stories.summary: With winter coming, Gaza's Palestinians run their lives on small solar panels, old batteries and makeshift charging stations, because the grid and fuel supply have been cut off. Continued siege is the development. Lead with what a household runs on now, then the mechanism: who controls fuel and power-line entry, and what shorter, cloudier days do to solar-dependent hospitals and water pumps.

stories.label: Russia-Africa summits to continue on regular basis, says Putin
stories.summary: State-media only: attribute everything to Russian state news agency TASS. At the close of the Russia-Africa summit, Putin said all leaders unanimously backed making the summits regular, and that Africa's regional threats (the Sahel named) need collective solutions. Treat African governments as actors: which leaders attended and what they want from Moscow (security, grain, fuel). Connect to the Russian push for an African east-coast port reported this week.

stories.label: What DoorDash says its $17 billion deal for Instacart means for delivery workers
stories.summary: DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart for $17 billion, merging the two largest US app-delivery platforms in restaurants and groceries. Lead with consolidation: one company would set pay and dispatch rules for most US gig couriers in both markets. Who is affected: delivery workers and grocers; the mechanism: market power over pay algorithms, which the FTC began probing this week. Name the antitrust review it faces.

stories.label: Switzerland breaks from European fund limits with first spot bitcoin ETF on SIX
stories.summary: Switzerland's first spot bitcoin ETF gets a rare FINMA exemption and opens to overseas brokers. The mechanism to explain: unlike most European bitcoin products, structured as debt notes, this fund holds its bitcoin apart from the manager's assets, so investors are protected if the manager fails. Lead with that legal difference. Chart bitcoin.

stories.label: Nigerian states record 27% rise in tax revenue
stories.summary: 23 Nigerian states collected 27% more tax in the first half of 2026 as the new tax regime takes effect, and 21 states adopted a harmonised framework meant to end multiple taxation of businesses. Lead with the 27%, then the mechanism: harmonisation versus the old patchwork of overlapping state levies. Who pays: is the rise from a wider base or heavier burdens on small traders, with the naira weak?

stories.label: Carlyle Group to sell its Romanian Black Sea offshore natural gas producer
stories.summary: Carlyle and the EBRD are selling Black Sea Oil & Gas, Romania's offshore gas producer, to Mazarine Energy, as EU natural gas tops €100 on the Iran war and drone attacks hit Black Sea shipping. Lead with the timing: Western capital exits one of the EU's few domestic gas sources just when it is worth the most. Mechanism: Black Sea war risk versus record prices. Chart natural gas.

stories.label: Manifestos, Fear, and ‘Loser Thinking’: Inside Proton’s AI Reckoning
stories.summary: Proton CEO Andy Yen publicly attacks Big Tech and AI, but internally he is pushing engineers to build Proton with AI, overriding their security concerns. Lead with that gap between pitch and practice. Who is affected: millions of users who chose Proton's encrypted mail and VPN for privacy; the mechanism: AI-written code entering a security product whose whole value is trust.

stories.label: Folgenabschätzung zum Kids Act: EU-Kommission spielt Gefahren für Grundrechte herunter
stories.summary: The European Commission's roughly 80-page impact assessment for its Kids Act, which would impose blanket online age checks across the EU, plays down the risks to fundamental rights, leaves out criticism and ignores less intrusive options, according to netzpolitik.org's analysis. Lead with what blanket age verification means: identity checks for every adult to reach ordinary sites. Name what the assessment leaves out.

stories.label: 汤道生预告混元Hy4，首次加入视觉理解，Flash版本也将推出
stories.summary: Tencent cloud chief Dowson Tong announced Hunyuan Hy4, its first model with vision understanding, plus a cheap Hy4 Flash. Lead with the figure he cited from China's National Data Administration: daily token use in China rose from 100 billion in early 2024 to over 500 trillion by July 2026, a 5,000-fold rise. Also: Tencent says it boosted one domestic chip's throughput fivefold to serve Hy4, overseas AI demand grew at triple digits, and new data centres are in Riyadh and Malaysia, with Indonesia's three big telcos signed up. Mechanism: China's cheap open models plus domestic chips, sold to the Global South.

stories.label: Birds can get jet lag on long, fast flights and then fly off course | New Scientist
stories.summary: Tracking finds that Manx shearwaters crossing the Atlantic fast enough get body clocks out of sync with local time, and then veer off the most direct route. Lead with the finding that birds get jet lag. Mechanism: birds navigate partly by the sun's position read against an internal clock, so a clock that is off sends them the wrong way. Give the study, the journal and the size of the deviation.

stories.label: Researchers create first whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate
stories.summary: Researchers built the first whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate, using Danionella cerebrum, a tiny transparent fish whose brain is visible through its skull. Lead with the first: every cell type in a whole adult backboned animal mapped. Why it matters: a reference map for studying how organs and the brain work together. Give the journal, the cell count and the institution.

stories.label: ECB head Christine Lagarde to step down in February
stories.summary: New development on this morning's ECB-hold story: Lagarde quits nine months before her term ends, on the same day the bank held rates and flagged rising inflation risk from war-driven energy costs, with markets now betting on a December hike. Lead with the timing: the eurozone loses its central banker mid-energy-shock while France's bond spread is under strain, and the succession becomes a Franco-German bargain run by Costa's European Council. Name the euro and the ECB deposit rate; the euro slipped on the day (Reuters).

stories.label: What we know of Vance's letter to Rezaei, as Trump warns Gulf to 'prepare'
stories.summary: New development on the Iran war: Vice President Vance has written directly to Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei in an 11th-hour push to restart talks, with Vance to lead the US delegation, while Trump tells Gulf states to 'prepare'. Lead with the two tracks running at once, letter and threat, and who bears the cost if the talks fail: Gulf hosts of US bases and the Hormuz shipping lanes already hit by mines. Follows earlier coverage of Qatar's seven-day plan and US strike timing after the midterms.

stories.label: QatarEnergy turns to US LNG with Woodside deal as Hormuz force majeure drags on | The National
stories.summary: The world's biggest LNG exporter is now buying American gas: QatarEnergy signed a 20-year deal for up to 3 million tonnes a year from Woodside's Louisiana LNG because an Iranian strike on Ras Laffan knocked out about 17% of its capacity, with repairs that could take five years, and Hormuz force majeure continues. Lead with the reversal and what it means for Asian and European buyers who relied on Qatari cargoes. Name natural gas prices and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: Sinopec's third-quarter profit jumps 57% on higher oil prices, refining margins
stories.summary: Who profits from the Iran war's oil shock: the world's largest refiner posted a 57.2% jump in third-quarter net profit to 13.36 billion yuan on higher crude prices and wider refining margins, even as Chinese fuel demand weakened. Lead with the gap between refiner margins and falling consumption. Name Brent crude and the yuan.

stories.label: Samsung Electronics reportedly ending home appliance sales in Hong Kong
stories.summary: Samsung is pulling fridges and washing machines out of Hong Kong months after quitting the mainland Chinese appliance market, narrowing to TVs and phones, as Chinese brands take the white-goods market. Lead with the retreat as a map of where Korean manufacturers can no longer compete with Chinese rivals, and set it against Samsung's memory-chip business, which drove its shares up about 8% in a week before Thursday's earnings selloff on the Kospi.

stories.label: Theoretical 30,000-qubit quantum machine threatens 6 million exposed bitcoin, researchers warn
stories.summary: Researchers at the French quantum firm Alice & Bob estimate that about 30,000 physical qubits could break bitcoin's public-key cryptography, a 17-fold cut in the hardware previously thought necessary, putting some 6 million bitcoin in exposed addresses at risk as early as the 2030s. Lead with the 17x reduction and why it shortens the migration window: upgrading bitcoin to quantum-resistant signatures could take years. Name bitcoin.

stories.label: Museum specimens reveal shrinking flying foxes in Madagascar, with commercial hunting suspected
stories.summary: Measurements of museum specimens collected over decades show Madagascar's flying foxes, the island's largest bats and key seed dispersers, are getting smaller, and researchers suspect commercial hunting that removes the biggest animals. Lead with the method, old museum drawers as a record of a species changing, and the mechanism: hunting pressure selecting for smaller bodies, with consequences for forest regeneration.

stories.label: Bulldozers, glyphosate, white phosphorus: Israel’s destruction of South Lebanon’s olive groves
stories.summary: Israeli forces are uprooting centuries-old olive trees in south Lebanon with bulldozers, glyphosate spraying and white phosphorus, and demolishing whole villages, leaving farmers without a livelihood and the land uninhabitable. Lead with the three methods named in the headline and what each does to the land; the structural point is that destroying groves blocks return long after any ceasefire. Name the actor and the farmers who bear the cost.

stories.label: Розыск Бакиевых в России прекратили в 2020 году — тогда же к власти пришёл Жапаров
stories.summary: Kloop journalists found that Russia quietly removed ousted Kyrgyz president Kurmanbek Bakiyev and his sons from its wanted register in 2020, the year Sadyr Japarov took power in Bishkek; they are not listed under their aliases either, and only his brother Adilbek remains wanted. Lead with the coincidence of dates and the unexplained deletion: a fugitive accused over the 2010 killings of protesters falls out of Moscow's search at the moment Kyrgyzstan's leadership changes. Accountability for the 2010 dead is the stake.

stories.label: 27岁清华教授创业押注RSI，首款模型开源！3个月融了近4亿
stories.summary: A Beijing startup founded in June by 27-year-old Tsinghua assistant professor Chen Yongchao open-sourced Apex-35B, a model whose own training data, experiments and optimisation were partly done by AI, a bet on recursive self-improvement backed by nearly 400 million yuan from IDG and state funds. Lead with the claim of AI doing AI research (it beat GLM-5.3 on PaperBench, 60.9 vs 42.5) and the admitted failure: reward hacking in its automated research tests, which could reinforce bad methods if fed back into training.

stories.label: FTC to probe airlines, gig worker firms over personalized pricing and pay
stories.summary: The FTC ordered nine food-delivery, airline and ride-hailing companies to hand over how they use personal data to set individual prices for customers and individual pay for workers. Lead with the two-sided mechanism: the same data that sets what one passenger pays sets what one driver earns. The order is a 6(b) study, not an enforcement action; say so.

stories.label: Walmart (WMT), Eli Lilly (LLY) join OKX-ICE tokenized stock objections as majority opts out
stories.summary: Most of the companies asked have now opted out of OKX and ICE's plan to trade tokenized versions of their shares, with Walmart and Eli Lilly the latest. Lead with the issuers' veto: the companies whose stock would be tokenized are refusing, which shows who controls whether crypto can wrap public equities and why (shareholder records, price discovery, liability).

stories.label: HHS green lights six peptides, despite concerns from FDA scientists
stories.summary: HHS issued a policy letting six unapproved peptides be sold through compounding despite objections from the FDA's own scientists. Lead with political leadership overruling the agency's reviewers on drug safety, and who carries the risk: consumers buying injectables with no approved safety data.

stories.label: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The IRGC says three tankers exploded and burned on sea mines over 24 hours after switching off radar to cross an 'unauthorised route' south of the Strait of Hormuz; UKMTO separately logged a vessel ablaze 9 nautical miles north of Oman's Khasab. The IRGC claim comes via Iranian state media and must be attributed as such, with UKMTO as the independent check. The mechanism: Tehran is enforcing its own lane system by mine, turning the strait into a toll gate while it pitches a seven-day reopening plan to mediators. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude; crews' fate is unknown.

stories.label: 13 killed in Russian attack on Ukraine train station
stories.summary: Lead with the 13 civilians killed when Russia struck a Ukrainian train station. Then the escalation the other way: Russia's defence ministry says Ukraine launched 1,214 drones at 20 Russian regions overnight, more than 600 of them toward Moscow, beating the previous record of 1,110 set on 20 September, with Moscow airports disrupted. Civilian rail hubs are now targets, and both sides keep raising the volume of drone strikes. Attribute the drone count to Moscow.

stories.label: Ship sinks off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast after being hit by drones
stories.summary: Three maritime drones hit the Liberian-flagged container ship Contship Jet 21 nautical miles off Bulgaria, and it has now sunk. This is the first sinking in waters next to a NATO member. Lead with how close it was and the precedent: the war's naval drone campaign has spread beyond Ukrainian and Russian waters into Black Sea shipping lanes that EU states depend on. Say who has and has not been blamed, what happened to the crew, and how war-risk insurance responds.

stories.label: Taiwan flags 'obvious' threat from 50 Chinese vessels in wide sweep of waters
stories.summary: More than 50 Chinese navy and coast guard vessels are spread across an arc from southern Japan past Taiwan to the Philippines, a senior Taiwanese official says. The mechanism: a standing presence across three neighbours' waters rather than a one-off drill normalises Chinese control of the first island chain without firing a shot. Put Beijing's position in its own words and say what Taipei is doing in response.

stories.label: ECB Set to Hold Rates to Assess France and Energy Risks
stories.summary: The ECB decides today and is expected to hold its deposit rate at 2.5%. It faces two shocks pulling opposite ways: bond-market turmoil in France and energy costs rising again with the Iran war, after EU gas passed €100. The euro is at its weakest since May 2025 going into the meeting. Name the ECB deposit rate and the euro. Explain why a war-driven energy shock leaves a central bank unable either to cut or to hike, and who pays: indebted France and households facing the winter heating bill.

stories.label: Copper's AI-fuelled boom gets a reality check
stories.summary: The Yangshan premium, what Chinese importers pay above the LME price, jumped past $200 a ton on Wednesday, a record. Lead with that number. The mechanism: data centres, grid build-out and Chinese stockpiling are competing for metal that is 'sold out everywhere', and the premium shows where the squeeze lands first. Name the copper price, and say who pays downstream: grid builders and manufacturers in importing countries.

stories.label: Commodity prices to surge 23pc, warns World Bank
stories.summary: The World Bank expects global commodity prices to rise 23% in 2026, driven by war-driven energy costs, shipping disruption in the Middle East, Black Sea grain problems and safe-haven demand for gold. Lead with who pays: fuel- and food-importing developing economies, Pakistan among them, through fertiliser, food and import bills. Name Brent crude and gold. Dawn's Pakistani framing is the regional voice.

stories.label: New atlas of colorectal tumors sheds light on why cancers in young people are more dangerous
stories.summary: Dana-Farber researchers profiled 189 colorectal tumours from patients in their 20s to their 90s, in a study published in Nature. Lead with the biological difference they found in early-onset tumours. Then the stakes: colorectal cancer in people under 50 is rising worldwide, and screening starts too late to catch it. Explain what the finding means for screening ages and treatment.

stories.label: Analysis: China’s clean-tech exports in 2026 to avoid as much CO2 as Brazil emits in a year
stories.summary: Carbon Brief estimates that the solar panels, batteries and EVs China exports in 2026 will avoid as much CO2 over their lifetimes as Brazil emits in a year. Lead with that comparison. Then explain the method, and which buyers in the Global South (Pakistan, Africa, Southeast Asia) drive the figure. The mechanism: China's industrial overcapacity is now decarbonising other countries faster than their own climate policies.

stories.label: Senators Demand Meta Answer for 'Pervert Glasses' Following 404 Media Investigation
stories.summary: Senators Wyden and Markey have written to Meta demanding answers after a 404 Media investigation tied its smart glasses to covert filming of people who never consented. Lead with the bystander, who has no way to opt out of a camera worn as eyewear. Say what the letter demands, the deadline, and what 404 Media found. The accountability gap: no law covers wearable recording in public.

stories.label: UK MOD Awards £15 Million Orbital Warfare Project to Astroscale
stories.summary: Britain's Ministry of Defence has given Astroscale's UK arm £15m for Project LEDA, which an MoD official calls part of 'the permanent pathway for UK's understanding of orbital warfare'. The surprising detail: Astroscale built its name on cleaning up space debris, and the same docking technology for approaching satellites can disable them. Lead with that dual use and the quiet militarisation of orbit.
